_why: Which printed cell on 433-A(OIC) is computed from which other printed cells. Read by run-form-gate.mjs step 11, which recomputes every entry FROM WHAT THE FILLED PDF PRINTS and compares it to the printed figure. No figure lives here except the ones the FORM ITSELF PRINTS as constants — the $1,000 on line (1), the $3,450 vehicle allowance on line (6b), and the .8 quick-sale multiplier that appears five times — and every one is quoted from the caption that prints it.
authored_from: The printed page text of adapters/pdf/forms/f433aoi.pdf, extracted from the content streams and read alongside the widget rectangles by adapters/pdf/align-block.mjs. Captions below are quoted verbatim. NOT from field names: ELEVEN leaf names on this form are known to be actively wrong about what their cell means — including the page-3 pair Total_Value_Vehicles_Attached[0] and Enter_Allowance[0], which are printed lines (6d) and (6e) respectively and so hold each other's job. One of the eleven — RetirementAcct2[0].CurrentMarketValue[0].Times_7[0] — is a feeder of entry (3a) QSV below, where the leaf says .7 and the page says .8.
_slice: PRINTED PAGES 1, 2 AND 3. Page 1 prints no total. Page 2’s eleven computed cells and page 3’s nine are all here. Pages 4-8 are not in this file yet; a printed total absent from both `totals` and `not_checkable` has not been declined, it has simply not been read.
_notes: THIS FILE EXISTS BECAUSE THE SCHEMA CAN NOW CARRY THE FORM. It was deliberately not authored during slice 2: the feeder schema then added and subtracted and had no factor and no constant, so (3a)'s X .8 and (1)'s minus $1,000 — the two cells on page 2 that most need checking — would have been the two it could not express. Nine clean passes printed beside two silently-absent checks is worse than a SKIP that says nothing was checked.

A FACTOR AND A CONSTANT, NOT AN EXPRESSION LANGUAGE. `factor` and `constant` are two numbers per feeder, and a feeder contributes sign x (factor x sum-of-its-cells + constant). That is enough for every printed formula on pages 1-3 that is not a conditional, and it is deliberately not enough to invent arithmetic here: this file can still only say which printed cells feed a line and by how much.

`floor` IS THE FORM'S OWN PRINTED INSTRUCTION, not a tolerance. Page 2 y 668.1 prints: 'Round to the nearest dollar. Do not enter a negative number. If any line item is a negative number, enter "0".' Only a line that subtracts a printed constant can go negative, so exactly two lines declare it: (1) on page 2 and (6b) on page 3, whose own caption repeats the instruction as '(If line (6a) minus $3,450 is a negative number, enter "0")'. When the floor actually fires the gate prints 'floored at 0.00' on that line, so a match that depended on it can never read as an unconditional match.

ROUNDING IS NOT MODELLED, AND THAT IS A KNOWN LIMIT. The same printed instruction says 'Round to the nearest dollar'. Comparison here is exact to the cent. A market value that is not a multiple of 5 makes X .8 land on a fraction of a dollar, and a correctly-rounded form would then disagree with this recomputation by up to 50 cents. The acceptance fixture uses multiples of 5 so this cannot mask a real defect, and the limit is recorded for Principal rather than papered over with a tolerance — a tripwire with slack in it is a tripwire that stops catching the small errors.

PER-ROW ENTRIES ARE NOT GROUP TOTALS. Eleven entries below address a single printed ROW via `total_cell` with a row index, because their printed caption states a formula across the cells of that one row — 'Current market value X .8 = [cell] - [cell] = (3a)'. A group total sums a column; these do not. Both shapes are in this file and they are told apart by `total_cell` versus `total_key`.

(2c) IS DECLARED CHECKABLE ON THE ARGUABLE READING. The map records it as a one-operand equation — the page draws an '=' between the dollar-equivalent cell and the (2c) marker and draws no other operator — with the case against stated: a lone '=' could be decoration on a row the taxpayer carries across by hand, in which case (2c) is plain input. Included here because the arithmetic is identical under both readings, so this entry cannot be the thing that makes a wrong answer look right. Still reported as arguable rather than resolved.

WHAT THE ATTACHMENT CELLS DO AND DO NOT PROVE. (1c), (2d), (3b), (4b-source) and (4b-loans) are declared not_checkable below: what they sum is on an attachment this engine never sees. They are nevertheless OPERANDS of (1), (2), (3), (4) and (4b), which ARE checkable — the page prints those cells, and a recomputation reads what the page prints. The rule is about where a formula's operands are PRINTED, not where their figures came from.

FIVE QUICK-SALE TRIPWIRES NOW, ACROSS TWO PAGES: (3a) on page 2 and (5a), (5b), (6a), (6c) on page 3. Every one of them is the same printed shape - a cell whose only identifying text is the ‘X .8 = $’ drawn immediately to its left, with nothing printed above it - and every one is checked against the market-value cell beside it rather than against any leaf name. Four of the five leaf names happen to say times_8 or Times_8; the fifth says Times_7 and carries the same printed X .8. That is why none of the five is bound or checked by name.

THE VEHICLE QUICK-SALE CELLS ARE UNCONDITIONAL AND THE VEHICLE TOTALS ARE NOT. The ‘if the vehicle is leased, enter 0 as the total value’ instruction is printed against ‘Total value of vehicle’, which is the (6a)/(6c) cell, NOT against the X .8 cell. So both vehicle quick-sale entries below are checked on every row whatever the lease answer, while (6a)/(6c) itself is declared not checkable.

(6e) IS NOT AN ALLOWANCE, WHATEVER ITS LEAF NAME SAYS. Enter_Allowance[0] is printed line (6e), ‘Total value of vehicles listed from attachment’ - attachment-sourced input, declared not checkable. The allowance on page 3 is the $3,450 printed at (6b) and (6d), which is a constant the form draws itself and therefore checkable at (6b).

TWO PRINTED CONDITIONALS ARE DECLINED RATHER THAN APPROXIMATED, and they are declined for different reasons. (6a)/(6c) branches on the row's own Lease/Own box, which IS printed here - one declarative predicate would recover it, and that is reported to Principal rather than built, because the schema change authorised for this slice was a factor and a constant. (6d) branches on whether the offer is joint, which is NOT recorded anywhere on this form's eight pages - no predicate over a printed cell could recover it, now or later. Recording the difference matters: the first is a gap that can close and the second never can.

totals.caption: X .8 = $
totals._the_tripwire: The cell this entry checks is topmostSubform[0].F433-A-OIC_Page2[0].RetirementAcct2[0].CurrentMarketValue[0].Times_7[0]. The leaf name says .7. The page says .8, drawn at x 154.7..184.7 immediately to the cell's left, and says it twice more on page 3. Binding by leaf name and multiplying by 0.7 would understate the quick sale value by 12.5% of market value AND still leave every printed total on the page reconciling, because (3a) and (3) would both be computed from the same wrong figure. This entry is the only thing on the form that reads the multiplier off the page.

That is why the column is named quick_sale_equity and not equity, and it is why this entry and the one above it are two separate checks: together they prove both halves of the row, and either alone would let a wrong multiplier through.

entries.printed_caption: Total of retirement accounts from attachment. [current market value X .8 minus loan balance(s)]
entries.review_page_advisory: THE X .8 IS IN THE CAPTION. The quick-sale discount applies to attached retirement accounts exactly as it does to the printed row at (3a), and a preparer who omits it understates the offer by 20% of attached market value with nothing on this page able to catch it. Surface this caption verbatim beside the value. The engine cannot verify an attachment; it can put the requirement in front of the person who can.

entries.printed_caption: Total value of property(s) from attachment [current market value X .8 minus any loan balance(s)]
entries.why_not_checkable: Attachment-sourced. Everything it sums is on an attachment this engine never sees. It is nevertheless an operand of (5), which IS checkable.
entries.review_page_advisory: THE X .8 IS IN THE CAPTION. Attached real property is quick-sale discounted exactly as the printed rows at (5a) and (5b) are, and the loan balance comes off AFTER the discount, not before. A preparer who nets the loan first, or who omits the discount, overstates or understates this figure with nothing on the page able to catch it.

entries.printed_caption: Total value of vehicle (if the vehicle is leased, enter 0 as the total value) = (6a) $ / (6c) $
entries.why_not_checkable: A PRINTED CONDITIONAL whose selector is the row’s own Lease/Own checkbox. The cell is quick sale value minus loan balance when Own is ticked and 0 when Lease is ticked. The feeder schema adds and subtracts printed money cells with a factor and a constant and has no predicate over a checkbox, so it cannot express ‘0 when leased’. Declared not checkable rather than checked-and-wrong: a tripwire that fired on every correctly-filled leased vehicle is a tripwire people would turn off. A single declarative predicate would recover it - reported to Principal, not built.
entries.review_page_advisory: CHECK THE LEASE BOX AGAINST THIS FIGURE BY HAND. If the row’s Lease box is ticked this cell must read 0, whatever the market value and loan balance beside it say. If Own is ticked it must read quick sale value minus loan balance - taken off the DISCOUNTED value, not off market value. Nothing in the automated checks looks at this cell, and the quick-sale multiplier on the same row is checked and tells you nothing about it.

entries.printed_caption: If you are filing a joint offer, subtract $3,450 from line (6c) / (If line (6c) minus $3,450 is a negative number, enter "0") / If you are not filing a joint offer, enter the amount from line (6c)
entries.why_not_checkable: A PRINTED CONDITIONAL WHOSE SELECTOR IS NOT ON THIS FORM AT ALL. The phrase ‘joint offer’ is drawn exactly once on all eight pages of 433-A(OIC) - here - and no cell anywhere records the answer; it is declared on Form 656, which this engine does not hold. Unlike (6a)/(6c), no predicate over a printed cell could recover this one.
entries.review_page_advisory: ANSWER THIS FROM FORM 656, NOT FROM MARITAL STATUS. On a joint offer this cell is line (6c) minus $3,450, floored at zero. On a separate offer it is line (6c) unchanged - the $3,450 is NOT applied twice across two vehicles on a separate offer. A married taxpayer may file a separate offer, so the Section 1 marital status on page 1 does not answer this and must not be used to.

entries.printed_caption: Total value of vehicles listed from attachment [current market value X .8 minus any loan balance(s)]
entries.why_not_checkable: Attachment-sourced, and INPUT rather than computed despite the leaf name Enter_Allowance[0]. It is an operand of (6), which IS checkable.
entries.review_page_advisory: THIS CELL IS NOT AN ALLOWANCE, whatever its field name suggests - it is the vehicles-from-attachment total, and THE X .8 IS IN ITS CAPTION. Attached vehicles are quick-sale discounted exactly as the printed rows are, and a leased vehicle on the attachment contributes 0 here just as it would at (6a)/(6c). The $3,450 allowance is applied at (6b) and (6d) and must NOT be applied again here.
